support_locator: Carpentry Basics discussion of spike marks/tape and color use for scenic locations
paraphrase_notes: Directly supports that spike/tape marks are normal stagecraft communication tools and that colors may be used to distinguish production-specific states or pieces.
applicability_notes: Local 193 training context only; exact colors and conventions vary by production.
required_qualifier: Do not present any color meaning as a universal national stagehand standard.

support_locator: Primer 20 stagehand skills including cable taping/tabbing
paraphrase_notes: Corroborates that tape handling is a legitimate entry-stagehand skill area.
applicability_notes: Local 122 training context only; does not define a universal marking code.
required_qualifier: Local training evidence establishes relevance, not universal meaning.

paraphrase_notes: Crew Blueprint deliberately separates temporary production marking from manufacturer/regulatory/inspection/safety labeling. Exact controlled-label requirements depend on the actual equipment, employer and regulation.
applicability_notes: Internal conservative boundary; no claim that one external rule covers every controlled label category.
required_qualifier: Where learner-facing content names a specific regulated or manufacturer label, attach the exact controlling source for that label type.

support_locator: Carpentry Basics definitions of flats, wagons, scenic movement and stagecraft mechanisms
paraphrase_notes: Directly supports that flats/wagons are established stagecraft categories and that scenery may be hand-moved or use other mechanisms depending on the system.
applicability_notes: Local training context; exact scenic-release workflow varies by production.
required_qualifier: Physical movability does not establish show-state release or permission to move a scenic piece.

paraphrase_notes: Crew Blueprint reserves fly, automation, powered scenic machinery, overhead attachment, structural acceptance and unassigned cue operation to separate specialist/employer authority.
applicability_notes: Internal conservative curriculum boundary. Exact specialist authority depends on the system, employer, venue and jurisdiction.
required_qualifier: Do not convert this boundary into operational fly, automation, rigging or machinery instruction.

paraphrase_notes: Supports awareness of dock-edge, surface and equipment-traffic hazards and the need for controlled movement around loading docks.
applicability_notes: OSHA eTool guidance; does not create a universal live-event dock workflow.
required_qualifier: Employer/site traffic plans and actual dock conditions control the work.

support_locator: OSHA pedestrian-traffic guidance around powered industrial trucks
paraphrase_notes: Directly supports pedestrian awareness of powered-equipment operating zones, visibility/blind-spot and rear-swing hazards.
applicability_notes: Pedestrian-awareness evidence only; no powered-equipment operating procedure is derived.
required_qualifier: The learner remains a pedestrian/general hand unless separately trained and authorized as an operator.

support_locator: 1910.176 clearances at loading docks, doorways, turns and passageways where mechanical handling equipment is used
paraphrase_notes: Corroborates the need for clear material-flow routes and sufficient clearance in covered material-handling areas.
required_qualifier: Do not infer one universal live-event traffic pattern from the regulation.

paraphrase_notes: Supports separating powered industrial-truck operator training/authorization from general pedestrian awareness. The broader Crew Blueprint boundary also includes MEWPs, vehicles, cargo acceptance and truck-pack authority that require separate evidence/authority layers.
applicability_notes: Powered industrial trucks within OSHA scope only.
required_qualifier: Do not cite 1910.178 as the source for vehicle, MEWP, driver, cargo or truck-pack rules outside its scope.

paraphrase_notes: Crew Blueprint intentionally places vehicle, powered-equipment, cargo and load-acceptance work outside the general dock-awareness route unless separately trained/authorized.
applicability_notes: Internal authority framing; each external activity retains its own legal/employer evidence.
required_qualifier: Course completion remains awareness only and does not traverse external operator/driver/load gates.
